> Aussiefied at **Swaggie** level, with **Dinkum** embellishment and **Dad** vulgarity. [Prefer docs that are as dry as a dead dingo's donger?](../plain/architecture/package-layout.md)

# Package layout

`aussiefy/` is one flat package whose modules fall into layers. Each layer may use the layers below it, never
the ones above. The layering is documented here and enforced by `tests/architecture/test_layers.py`, rather than by
subpackages (see [DD-006](decisions/dd-006-layered-flat-package.md)).

| Layer | Modules |
|---|---|
| Public API | `__init__.py` (translate, translate_changes, lookup, lint, guide, plan, bulldust, yarn, Translator, load_dictionary, verify, and the result and error types) |
| Surfaces (thin adapters) | `cli.py`, `mcp_server.py`, `skills/aussiefy/SKILL.md` |
| Toolkit | `harness.py` (seven agent operations), `bulldust.py` (constructor operation boundary), `lookup.py`, `lint.py`, `guide.py`, `verify.py` (fidelity and policy checks), `align.py` (shared sentence counterparts), `retelling.py` (agent-neutral briefs, JSON Schema tool contracts, sessions, dispatch and checked submission) |
| Document translation | `translation.py` (shared surface routing), `markdown.py` (strict source spans and document results), `markup.py` (extended Markdown/MDX scanning) |
| Optional API clients | `yarn.py` (built-in retelling loop and Anthropic tool adapter), `llm.py` (surface and sentence rewrites), `claude.py` (Anthropic SDK boundary) |
| Engine | `engine.py` (the pipeline), `text.py`, `matcher.py`, `detect.py`, `degree.py` (reviewed degree composition), `semantic_checks.py` (pure bounded source-aware meaning, composition and known-theme checks), `select.py`, `grammar.py` (declared output requirements), `realise.py`, `morph.py`, `garnish.py`, `constructions.py` (pure typed composition), `quiz.py` (pure gloss, eligibility and seeded distractor selection), `context.py`, `nominal_modifiers.py` (lexical noun modifiers and written cardinal evidence), `meaning_context.py` (typed source meaning conditions), `policy.py`, `genre.py` (pure form policy and classification), `dialect.py` (source-English swaps), `pos.py` (bundled tagger), `protected.py` (opaque source spans and restoration), `changes.py` (every change, its alternatives rendered in place, in the same pass) |
| Dictionary | `schema.py` (entries, concepts), `entry_ids.py` (permanent public keys, alias validation and continuity), `fences.py` (scoped phrase protections and validation), `evidence.py` (stored evidence, pure attestation scoring and shared usage gates), `themes.py` (reviewed tag tiers and immutable subject policy), `cards.py` (the entry cards lookup and the changes builder both show), `masks.py` (the maskable words in a rendering), `model.py` (the dictionary as data, and what derives from it), `loader.py` (reading and validating the YAML), `construction_data.py` (construction catalogue validation), `terms.py` (when two spellings are one term), `dump.py` |
| Similarity | `embed.py`, `static.py` (the bundled model), `models.py` (installed ones) |
| Maintainers | `gaps.py`, `explain.py`, `rounds.py` (research rounds), `judge.py` (blind packets, report validation and optional Claude boundary), `scrape/` (scrape, fragments, harvest, tag, review) |
| Shared | `errors.py` (`UserError`, the error a user can fix) |

`recognition.py` belongs to the Engine layer: it reads source-owned Australian terms through the shared
meaning and grammar checks. `personal_terms.py` validates request-owned wording without I/O or dictionary
mutation. The shared pass activates source ownership in frozen v4; selection uses its actual edit traces.

`profile.py` belongs to the Engine layer: it validates immutable request\-local tunin''n applies it to the
selected level'n swearin' profiles without changing dictionary data. The data the engine reads is in
`aussiefy/data/` (see [the dictionary](../functional/dictionary.md)).

`vocabulary.py` belongs to the Dictionary layer. It composes raw entry/concept additions'n explicit
versioned patches before the loader builds one validated dictionary'n its indexes. Anyway, it performs no I/O;
the loader owns files, source sidecars'n diagnostics. No overlay matching occurs during translation.

## The layering rule

The core (the engine, the dictionary and the similarity modules other than `models.py`) imports nothing from
the toolkit, the LLM modes, the surfaces or the maintainer tools, so it stays usable and testable on its own.
`tests/architecture/test_layers.py` checks this with an import scan, and allows one exception: `embed.make_embedder("local")`
resolves the installed model's settings through `models.py`, the one place the core reaches out. A second test
keeps the dictionary model (`model.py`, `schema.py`, `cards.py`, `policy.py`, `matcher.py`, `text.py`, `genre.py`) free of the loader's
file I/O.

`extensions.py` composes additive community evidence and validates same-sense collisions, while
`identifiers.py` owns the shared id grammar. `adjustments.py` validates contextual weight data and performs
pure bounded queries; it imports no selection or evidence-scoring code. `tuning.py` belongs to the Engine
layer: it validates per-call preference inputs, resolves exact keys before latest same-root fallbacks, and
combines personal weights with community factors on already eligible candidates. It performs no I/O and
changes no evidence or eligibility. `dictionary_identity.py` is loader
I/O and fingerprints file inputs. The model stores its result and never imports that I/O module.

Well, optional heavy dependencies \(anthropic, mcp, sentence\-transformers, torch\) are imported lazily, inside the
functions that need them, so the core imports'n runs with its core dependencies, offline. Markdown's light parser
heaps only in that mode; the plain engine never imports its adapter \([DD-015](decisions/dd-015-source-preserving-markdown.md)).

## Where to change things

- New slang, a new concept or a different level behaviour: the data in `aussiefy/data/`, not the code.
- A new way of detectin' or realisin' a meaning: the engine stage that owns it \([pipeline](pipeline.md)).
- A new agent-facing operation or parameter: the toolkit function first, then each surface, which
  `tests/functional/test_interfaces.py` holds in step.
- Anything that talks to Claude: through `claude.py`, the single seam for the SDK.
- Shared agent workflow or submission rules: `retelling.py`; client\-specific tool shapes'n model calls
  belong at the edge. See [DD-023](decisions/dd-023-agent-neutral-retelling.md).

Genre configuration'n the POS vocabulary are loaded once into the selected dictionary. Anyway, the classifier and
model derive values without opening files. Syntax scanners supply opaque source spans to the engine; yeah, but nah
Markdown/JSX rules enter its core. See [DD-016](decisions/dd-016-reconcile-source-capabilities.md).

`imagery.py` belongs to the core: it selects reviewed contextual images using dictionary data'n existin'
subject/slot grammar. Engine insertion'n toolkit suggestions share eligibility; bare lookup exposes
unbound templates. See [DD-025](decisions/dd-025-contextual-imagery.md).

`fence_readings.py` builds counterfactual explanation evidence in the core, using the shared engine's
source readings and eligible candidates. It performs no I/O and never changes the dictionary or removes
a protection. The maintainer command `scripts/audit_fences.py` serialises its results and missing-effect
diagnostics. Lookup builds and reuses individual protections through a dictionary-local bounded index;
the batch audit uses the same evidence. Ordinary translation does not invoke this build.
`discovery_outcomes.py` owns the shared discovery codes and imports no package modules. Rich discovery
cards are shared by lookup and entry details; changes-v3 uses the same card projection, themes and maker rules.

Bloody hell, lookup explicitly requests query\-fragment readings from `detect.py`; ordinary replacement detection keeps
its stricter default. Anyway, lookup owns the bounded whole\-query scope decision'n uses local canonical readings
as evidence, rather than treatin' every matched noun or modifier as a complete parse.

`names.py` owns the reviewed name catalogue'n deterministic, clean handle assembly in the core.
`explore.py` is the toolkit boundary for stable pages, stuffed cards, random entries'n name suggestions.
Fair dinkum, construction variations reuse the constructor boundary in `bulldust.py`, validating each complete expression
with the other parts held fixed. They don't create a second policy or splice implementation.


`cards.py` owns rich entry/riff metadata and attributable maker projection. `v3_contract.py` owns
construction/imagery cards and semantic response checks: source/dictionary identity, unique option keys,
selected membership, local span joins and provenance. The accepted draft assets remain historical;
real producers share these functions. `errors.py` owns string-compatible coded warnings and `tuning.py`
assigns preference codes at their origin.

`pins.py` is pure engine data'n validation for exact\-source replay packets. It retains immutable
entry forms, complete construction recipes'n canonical riffs. Stone the crows, it doesn't choose meanings, render
text, store share links or import the toolkit. Well, the ordinary engine rechecks hard eligibility; the
changes builder exposes optional replay sidecars outside the v3 response. `offsets.py` owns exact
edit\-coordinate maps shared by article/case/phonetic trackin''n change restoration. Document adapters
own Markdown escapin''n global source offsets.
